name: Hastings

licensing.selective: No selective licensing scheme in force that could be confirmed. The 2015 to 2020 scheme covering seven wards (Braybrooke, Castle, Central St Leonards, Gensing, Old Hastings, Ore and Tressell) ended in October 2020, and the government refused the council's application to renew it in 2021.

housing: Hastings and St Leonards is a hilly seaside town with one of the highest shares of private renting outside the big cities. Much of the rented stock is in large Regency and Victorian houses in the town centre and Central St Leonards that have been split into flats and bedsits, many on steep streets close to the sea. The Old Town has historic cottages and timber-framed houses, while Hollington, Baird and Ore have post-war estates. A selective licensing scheme ran in seven central wards from 2015 to 2020.
checkinTips: Regency and Victorian houses split into flats in St Leonards and the town centre: photograph each flat's door, meters, fire doors, alarms and the shared hallway and stairs.
Seafront homes: look for salt corrosion on window frames, balcony rails and door furniture, and damp on exposed walls.
Hillside homes on steep streets: photograph steps, sloping paths, retaining walls and any cracking, which can come from ground movement.
Old Town cottages: record beams, low doorways, uneven floors, open fireplaces and any damp in basements or rear walls.
Sash windows in period conversions: photograph cords, locks, cracked panes and any rot.
tenantHelp: Tenants with disrepair, damp or safety problems in a private let can contact Hastings Borough Council's housing renewal (private sector housing) team, after first reporting the problem to their landlord.
